what.text: Retatrutide is an experimental injected peptide from Eli Lilly, also called LY3437943. It acts on three hormone receptors at once: GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon. It is given once a week under the skin in trials.

Jastreboff et al., TRIUMPH-1, N Engl J Med

what.text: It is not approved anywhere the search checked. FDA says it is not a part of any FDA-approved drug and has not been found safe and effective for any condition.

research.text: Retatrutide has been tested in randomized trials paid for by Eli Lilly. The main ones are listed below as they were run. Lilly’s Phase 3 program is called TRIUMPH.

research.title: Phase 2: weight in adults with obesity

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, several dose groups
338 adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 to under 30 with at least one weight-related condition. 51.8% were men.
weekly retatrutide injections at 1, 4, 8 or 12 mg, or placebo
48 weeks
percent change in body weight at 24 weeks (main goal) and at 48 weeks

research.found: At 48 weeks, average weight changed by -8.7% on 1 mg, -17.1% on 4 mg, -22.8% on 8 mg and -24.2% on 12 mg, versus -2.1% on placebo. Side effects were mostly stomach and bowel effects and rose with dose. Heart rate rose with dose, peaked at 24 weeks and then fell. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04881760.

src.label: Jastreboff et al., retatrutide phase 2 in obesity, N Engl J Med

research.title: Phase 2: type 2 diabetes

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled (dulaglutide 1.5 mg)
281 adults with type 2 diabetes, on diet and exercise alone or metformin
weekly retatrutide (0.5 to 12 mg), dulaglutide or placebo
36 weeks
change in HbA1c (long-term blood sugar) at 24 weeks

research.found: At 24 weeks, HbA1c fell by up to 2.02 points on retatrutide (12 mg), versus 0.01 on placebo and 1.41 on dulaglutide. At 36 weeks, weight fell by up to 16.94% on retatrutide versus 3.00% on placebo. Mild to moderate stomach and bowel effects were reported in 35% on retatrutide, 13% on placebo and 35% on dulaglutide. There was no severe low blood sugar and no deaths. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04867785.

src.label: Rosenstock et al., retatrutide phase 2 in type 2 diabetes, Lancet

research.title: TRIUMPH-1: obesity without diabetes, with knee and sleep-apnea substudies

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
2,339 adults with obesity and no diabetes, including 574 with knee osteoarthritis and 243 with obstructive sleep apnea
weekly retatrutide 4, 9 or 12 mg, or placebo
80 weeks
percent change in body weight; knee pain score; breathing pauses during sleep (apnea-hypopnea index)

research.found: Average weight changed by -17.6% (4 mg), -23.7% (9 mg) and -25.0% (12 mg), versus -3.9% on placebo. Knee pain scores and breathing pauses fell more on retatrutide than placebo. The most common side effects were stomach and bowel effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05929066.

src.label: Jastreboff et al., TRIUMPH-1, N Engl J Med
Grunstein et al., TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA, N Engl J Med
TRIUMPH-1 trial record, ClinicalTrials.gov

research.title: TRIUMPH-2: obesity with type 2 diabetes

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
1,152 adults with a BMI of 27 or more and type 2 diabetes; mean age 55; 52% men
weekly retatrutide 4, 9 or 12 mg, or placebo
80 weeks
percent change in body weight

research.found: Average weight changed by -11.9% (4 mg), -16.8% (9 mg) and -18.8% (12 mg), versus -5.1% on placebo. Diarrhea, nausea, low blood pressure and abnormal skin sensations (dysesthesia) were more common on retatrutide. 12% on 9 mg and 8% on 12 mg stopped for good because of side effects or death, versus 5% on placebo. Investigators judged all deaths unrelated to the drug. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05929079.

src.label: TRIUMPH-2, Lancet
TRIUMPH-2 trial record, ClinicalTrials.gov

research.title: Type 2 diabetes on diet and exercise alone

facts.v: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
537 adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled by diet and exercise
weekly retatrutide 4, 9 or 12 mg, or placebo
40 weeks
change in HbA1c; percent change in body weight

research.found: HbA1c fell by 1.69 to 1.94 points on retatrutide and 0.81 on placebo. Weight changed by -11.5% to -15.3% versus -2.6%. 2% to 5% stopped retatrutide because of side effects. No severe low blood sugar was reported. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06354660.

src.label: Retatrutide alone in type 2 diabetes, phase 3, Lancet

research.text: Other Phase 3 trials are listed on ClinicalTrials.gov: TRIUMPH-3 (obesity and heart disease, 1,946 people, completed), TRIUMPH-4 (knee osteoarthritis, 445 people, completed), and a heart and kidney outcomes trial of about 10,000 people due to finish in 2029. Their full results were not found in journals as of November 1, 2026.

us.text: Retatrutide is not FDA approved for any use. FDA says it cannot be used in compounding, and that products sold "for research purposes" are being sold illegally. Lilly has sued sellers of products said to contain it. As of November 3, 2026.
Drugs@FDA has no record of an approved retatrutide product.

us.text: On August 12, 2026, Eli Lilly and Company, which is developing retatrutide, filed six lawsuits in federal courts against sellers of products said to contain it. In the complaints it filed, Lilly alleges that the “research use only” label is a pretext and that the products are illegal drugs sold for human use. Each of those complaints pleads state unfair-competition and consumer-protection claims; a law firm reports that Lilly asks for permanent injunctions, disgorgement of profits and attorney’s fees, and that only the Aesthetic Envy case adds a federal false-advertising claim. These are Lilly’s allegations; no court has ruled on them. Statuses are as of November 3, 2026, from the court records that could be opened.

us.text: A separate case concerns how FDA classifies retatrutide. In Eli Lilly and Company v. Kennedy (S.D. Ind., No. 1:24-cv-01503), Lilly challenged FDA’s refusal to treat retatrutide as a biological product. On September 30, 2025 the court upheld FDA’s finding that retatrutide is not a “protein,” but set aside its finding that retatrutide is not “analogous” to one, ruling that FDA “must revisit its determination” on that point. A reported appeal could not be confirmed from a court record.

src.label: Order on cross-motions for summary judgment, Lilly v. Kennedy (S.D. Ind.), GovInfo

us.text: FDA says it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved drugs containing retatrutide and other GLP-1 drugs, falsely labeled for research or not for human consumption. The letters below were opened on fda.gov. In each, FDA treats the retatrutide products as unapproved new drugs; the September 2025 letters add that retatrutide cannot be used in compounding because it “is not the subject of an applicable USP or NF monograph, is not a component of an FDA-approved human drug, and does not appear on the 503A bulks list.”

after.text: Retatrutide is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List. The 2026 List's class S0 (non-approved substances) bans, at all times, any drug that is not covered by another section of the List and has no current approval from any government health regulator for human use. It names drugs still in clinical development as an example. The 2027 List keeps this class and adds peptides to its examples. The search found no approval for retatrutide anywhere, so that class’s wording may cover it. WADA has not ruled on it. USADA says approved GLP-1 medicines are not prohibited.
